Everything runs on this device: audio is decoded from your video, recognised by Whisper (whisper.cpp) and translated to English, and the results are cached so a movie is never processed twice. Live Floating Subtitles treat the sound they hear the same way, in memory only. Nothing you watch or hear is uploaded. The internet is used only by the built-in browser, to load the websites you open, the same way any browser does; the app has no account, no ads and no analytics.

Play a video on a website, then tap Start AI subtitles. New tabs open a directory of foreign video sites (also in the menu); type in the address bar to go anywhere else.

If the video has its own subtitle or caption track, the app translates those captions into English on the phone and keeps their timing exactly. Otherwise it listens to the video's sound inside the browser and draws English subtitles over the video, about one to three seconds after the words. Nothing is recorded or uploaded.

Smart Delay (the timer button, up to 60 seconds): the video waits until that many seconds ahead are in English, after starting and after each jump, then plays with subtitles. It works with captions, and with the video's sound on most sites: their players load the sound some seconds ahead of the picture, and the app recognises what is already loaded. How far ahead depends on the site: if its player loads only 30 seconds, the app cannot be more than 30 seconds ahead. Where the sound can only be heard as it plays, live subtitles are used and Smart Delay cannot wait.

Protected (DRM) videos and videos the website does not let other pages read cannot be heard this way. You can then choose internal audio (Android asks for permission to capture the sound) or the microphone. The app never switches source without asking.
